skills.name: ai-fluency-culture-starter-kit
skills.description: Help People teams build a practical, human-centered AI fluency program with readiness questions, competencies, manager practices, performance-review prompts, guardrails, and rollout actions. Use when an organization is moving from informal AI experimentation to responsible, repeatable adoption.

skills.name: change-announcement-playbook
skills.description: Plan and draft the sequenced communications for a significant organizational change, a reorg, a leadership change or hard news. Builds the audience-by-audience plan so leaders, then managers, then employees hear in the right order, drafts the layered announcement and FAQ, the manager cascade pack and executive rehearsal notes, rehearses all-hands questions, drafts reduction scripts only after HR and legal sign off, and plans the follow-up communications. Use when someone is about to announce a change to the organization and needs the messages, order and owners. Not for deciding the change itself, for each manager's own team conversation, or for measuring how the change landed.

skills.name: company-specific-manager-coach
skills.description: Coach managers through feedback, development, prioritization, and people conversations using company principles and available employee context. Use before a 1:1, difficult conversation, performance review, or career discussion.

skills.name: development-conversation-partner
skills.description: Prepare for and follow up on a career conversation between a manager and a report. It turns the person's own aspirations and recent work into a prep brief, open questions, a short pre-read, practice for hard moments, a written plan both people own, and draft development goals with check-in dates. Use when a manager is planning a growth-focused 1:1, a year-end or mid-year career conversation, or has notes from one that need to become a plan, or when an employee is getting ready to raise their own career. It does not decide or predict promotion, level, pay or role outcomes.

skills.name: executive-people-strategy-brief
skills.description: Draft an evidence-backed leadership summary of people signals, goals progress, update themes, feedback themes and review cycle status, with options and owners for leaders to decide. Use when an executive, VP or HR leader wants a periodic people brief, a leadership pre-read or an evidence pack for a strategy discussion and wants it grounded in what they can see in Lattice or in exports they paste. Not a restructure plan.

skills.name: feedback-and-recognition
skills.description: Draft specific, behavior-grounded feedback or recognition that still sounds like the sender, check it for vague or biased wording, choose who sees it, and post it to Lattice only after the sender approves the exact text and visibility. Use when someone wants to give feedback to a report or peer, word a tricky point, rewrite a "great job" into real praise, thank a person or a group, write a milestone or farewell note, ask for feedback, work through hard feedback they received, or run a bias check on a pasted draft.

skills.name: goal-tracking-digest
skills.description: Build a recurring, goal-centered digest of where goals stand, with evidence for every status, the blockers people have written down, and drafts of progress summaries, goal refreshes and owner nudges. Use when a manager asks how their team's goals are doing or wants goal cards before 1:1s, when a leader wants a mid-quarter "where are our goals" check across their organization, when HR wants stale-goal reminders for a goal program, or when someone wants to summarize progress on their own goals and refresh them. Read-only by default. Never changes a goal without approval.

skills.name: grow-track-starter-kit
skills.description: Guide HR and People teams through the decisions required to design a useful competency structure in Lattice Grow. Use when an organization is starting, simplifying, or refreshing Grow tracks and needs a thought partner before drafting content.

skills.name: headcount-and-capacity-planner
skills.description: Model staffing and workload options against business goals. Builds a baseline of roles, open requisitions and committed work, compares flat, growth and constrained scenarios with stated assumptions, ties each requested role to a goal or workload driver, sequences requests, and drafts a finance submission, a plan-versus-actual tracker and a reforecast note. Use when a manager, leader, executive or HR partner is building, defending, reforecasting or tracking a headcount or capacity plan for a team or org. Not for choosing who stays or goes, not a restructure plan and not a leadership people brief.

skills.name: internal-move-navigator
skills.description: Help an employee or manager explore an internal move before it is decided, such as a lateral move, a stretch role or a critical internal role. Reflects on what is prompting the idea, sets the person's own evidence against a role description they paste, builds a bridge plan, prepares the conversation with their current manager and the people worth talking to, and plans for staying or moving. Use when someone says "I saw an internal opening", "I want a bigger role here", "I feel stuck but don't want to leave" or "how do I explore a move without a job-board mindset". It is not a candidate screen and never predicts approval, level or pay.

skills.name: internal-role-transition
skills.description: Plan one person's move to a new role or team inside the company. Drafts a handoff plan for the work they leave, stakeholder introductions for the new role, and an updated-expectations conversation guide, with a two-manager checklist. Use when an employee, their current manager or their new manager says someone is changing teams, managers or roles internally. Not for a manager taking over a team or for a company-wide reorganization.

skills.name: ma-integration-planner
skills.description: Plan the people side of a merger or acquisition. Builds a phased integration workplan with owners, decision gates and a specialist question log, an approach for harmonizing roles, levels, performance reviews and goals, a role-based retention checklist, day-one communications, and 30/60/100-day health checks. Use when someone says they are acquiring, merging with, or being integrated into another company and need to keep the people the deal was for.

skills.name: manager-capacity-review
skills.description: Show where manager workload is unsustainable across an org, using spans of control, layers, recent team growth and review-cycle timing, and draft a leadership proposal on spans, deadlines and manager support. Treats manager burnout as a system and structure problem, not a personal one. Use when a manager of managers, HR partner or executive wants a quarterly manager-load check, a pre-review-cycle check, or a check after a reorg or fast hiring. Not for scoring individual managers, for reorg option modelling, or for portfolio staffing and headcount scenarios.

skills.name: manager-transition-brief
skills.description: Build a per-person and team brief for someone who has just inherited a team, been promoted to lead one, or is covering for a leader, then draft first-1:1 agendas and a how-I-work note. Use when the user says they are taking over a team, have just become a manager or a manager of managers, are covering for a leader, or are preparing a handover brief for an incoming manager. Hands off to 1:1 Preparation for every 1:1 after the first.

skills.name: new-hire-manager-brief
skills.description: Prepare a manager for a new direct report's first week with one brief covering the expectations to set out loud, who the new hire should meet and why, and a dated first-week action checklist by owner. Use when a manager says someone is starting on their team soon, asks how to get ready for a new hire, or wants expectations, introductions and a first-week checklist. It does not build the 30/60/90 plan, pre-boarding message sequences or announcements.

skills.name: new-manager-enablement
skills.description: Help someone who is managing people for the first time, whether promoted or hired in, build their own first 90 days as a manager. Drafts a listen, align, adjust plan, a listening agenda for the team and for their own manager, a short list of manager development goals, upward-feedback questions for days 30 and 90, and weekly check-in prompts ending in a 90-day reflection. Use when the user says they were just promoted to manager, are leading a team for the first time, or asks for a new-manager 90-day plan, listening sessions or a first-time-manager routine. Not for taking over an existing team's history (use Manager Transition Brief) and not for a new hire's own onboarding plan.

skills.name: one-on-one-preparation
skills.description: Prepare a focused, context-aware one-on-one agenda using goals, updates, feedback, prior meetings, and development context. Use before a recurring 1:1, growth conversation, performance discussion, or follow-up meeting.

skills.name: performance-evidence-log
skills.description: Keep a manager's running, dated evidence log for each direct report, built from 1:1s, meetings, updates, feedback and goals, and turn it into a review-ready brief at the start of a review cycle. Use weekly, after a notable event, when feedback has gone quiet for someone, and whenever a review or calibration is coming up and the manager wants a sourced performance narrative instead of relying on memory. Use the Performance Review Drafting & Quality Check skill to write the review itself.

skills.name: performance-review-drafting-quality-check
skills.description: Draft or improve a performance review using goals, updates, feedback, 1:1 context, and prior reviews, then check it for evidence, clarity, balance, bias, and completeness. Use for self, peer, upward, or manager reviews.

skills.name: personalized-30-60-90-day-plan
skills.description: Draft a role-specific 30/60/90-day plan for a new hire or internal mover, with learning, relationship and delivery milestones, success criteria, support the manager commits to, optional starter goals and talking points for the first check-ins. Use when a manager says someone is starting on their team, asks for a 30/60/90 or onboarding plan for a specific role and level, or needs to set early expectations for a transfer or promotion. Written for the new hire and their manager. For a manager who is taking over a whole team, use Manager Transition Brief instead.

skills.name: post-review-growth-plan
skills.description: Help someone who has just received their own review or feedback turn it into a short, honest growth plan. It finds the themes, separates patterns from one-off comments, links growth themes to the expectations for their level, and drafts one to three development actions with milestones and check-in dates, plus an optional thank-you note to reviewers. Use when a person says they got their review back and asks what it means, what to work on, or how to turn it into a plan. It starts after the review is delivered. It does not write or evaluate a review, and it is for the person who received the feedback, not for a manager preparing a conversation about a report.

skills.name: promotion-readiness-packet
skills.description: Assemble the documented evidence for one person against their written next-level expectations and draft a manager-reviewed promotion case in the company's nomination format. Use when a manager is preparing a promotion nomination for a report, an employee is preparing their own case for their manager to review, a promotion window is approaching, or someone was told "not yet" and needs the evidence gaps named. It builds a case from documents. It never says whether someone should be promoted.

skills.name: reorganization-planner
skills.description: Plan an internal restructure that a leader or HR business partner has decided to explore. Lays out two to three structure options with scored trade-offs, maps the people impact of each, and produces the four plan artifacts, a change plan, a stakeholder map, a dependency map and a timeline, plus a decision memo, per-manager hand-off checklists and a goal and HRIS change list. Use when someone says they are restructuring a function, combining teams, changing spans or layers, or needs a reorg decision memo. Not for acquisitions or for stepping into a team someone else led.

skills.name: return-to-work-reboarding
skills.description: Draft a respectful return plan for someone coming back after an absence of two weeks or more, built only from the work. It covers a what-changed brief, a phased ramp the manager and the returner agree on, a first-week-back 1:1 agenda, a previewed list of goal and priority changes, and check-ins. Use when a manager, the returning employee or an HR partner says someone is returning from leave or a long absence. Never asks about or infers why the person was away.

skills.name: skill-gap-and-development-plan
skills.description: Compare a person's documented skills and recent work with the expectations of a target role or next level, then build a growth plan around two or three gaps. Use when an employee says they want to grow or asks what the next level really requires, or when a manager is preparing a career or development conversation with a report. Also use to re-check a plan from a prior quarter. This is a development map, not a promotion decision, and it never rates readiness.

skills.name: team-skills-gap-map
skills.description: Map a team's capability gaps against next quarter's priorities and suggest shared learning, stretch work and, when a gap cannot be closed internally, the evidence for a hiring or budget ask. Use when a manager or manager of managers is doing quarterly planning, after a priorities shift or reorg, or asks what skills the team is missing for the work ahead. This maps capabilities across the team. It never ranks, scores or compares the people on it, and a gap is never a performance judgment.

skills.name: team-structure-review
skills.description: Plan how two or more teams merge, or one team splits, as a structure question. Maps the current teams, lays out two to three structure options with trade-offs and transition cost, assigns responsibilities and decision owners so nothing is orphaned or doubled, aligns working norms and the recurring meeting load, runs an equity check before any person is discussed, and drafts a transition timeline and handoff list. Use when a manager, leader or HR partner says teams are merging, a team is being split, a lead layer may be added or reports may be rebalanced. Never says who should lead, move or stay. Not for company-wide reorganizations, acquisitions or taking over a team.

skills.name: weekly-updates-workflow
skills.description: Draft a clear, evidence-based weekly update from notes, goals, work systems, and Lattice context. Supports user-led, evidence-assist, evidence-first, manager/team roll-up, and optional scheduled-reminder workflows.
